paper_metadata.title: Real Option Pricing using Quantum Computers

experiments.description: Quantum accelerated Monte Carlo pricing of European-style derivatives using the standard square-root encoding and modified iterative quantum amplitude estimation (mIQAE) on a simplified Black-Scholes one-step simulation.

algorithm.variant: QAMC with square-root encoding and mIQAE
algorithm.convergence_criteria: Target precision ϵ and confidence level 1−γ; mIQAE run until the desired precision is reached.

problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate discounted expected payoff E[F(ST)|Ft] for European payoffs under Black-Scholes dynamics using square-root payoff encoding.

problem_instance.description: European vanilla call, vanilla put, and digital option pricing under Black-Scholes dynamics.

dataset_specification.description: Black-Scholes model with exact one-step simulation; no external dataset.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Discretize the Black-Scholes distribution into 32 points between 0.01 and 5.0; prepare the path-generation oracle US=UBS.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Estimate pricing error versus discretized expectation; report medians and 25/75 percentiles over repeated runs.

speedup_claims.conditions: assuming amplitude estimation is used and oracle cost is comparable; error scales as O(1/NQ) versus O(1/sqrt(NC))
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper notes hardware limitations and that the quantum gates are currently much slower than classical ones; the speedup is in query complexity, not wall-clock time.

experiments.description: Naive quantum accelerated Monte Carlo pricing of a negative-payoff linear derivative using the standard square-root encoding and mIQAE, demonstrating failure due to absolute-value effects.

algorithm.variant: Naive QAMC with square-root encoding and mIQAE for negative payoff
algorithm.convergence_criteria: Target precision ϵ and confidence level 1−γ; mIQAE run until the desired precision is reached.

problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate discounted expected payoff for F(ST)=ST−K using square-root encoding without separating positive and negative parts.

problem_instance.description: Linear payoff option with potentially negative values.

dataset_specification.description: Black-Scholes one-step simulation; payoff F(ST)=ST−K with K=1.5St.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Same Black-Scholes discretization and oracle preparation as the standard QAMC experiment.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Compare absolute error against discretized expectation; observe lack of convergence.

speedup_claims.conditions: naive square-root encoding applied to a payoff that can be negative
speedup_claims.caveats: The figure shows lack of convergence due to absolute-value effects in the encoding.

experiments.description: Quantum accelerated Monte Carlo pricing of a negative-payoff linear derivative using square-root encoding with explicit positive/negative payoff decomposition and mIQAE.

algorithm.variant: QAMC with square-root encoding, positive/negative decomposition, and mIQAE
algorithm.convergence_criteria: Target precision ϵ and confidence level 1−γ; separate amplitude estimation runs for positive and negative parts.

problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate F(ST)=F+(ST)−F−(ST), where F+(ST)=max(F(ST),0) and F−(ST)=|min(F(ST),0)|, then combine the two estimates.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Problem split into positive and negative codomains; separate estimation and recombination.

problem_instance.description: Linear payoff option with negative regions, priced by decomposing into positive and negative parts.

dataset_specification.description: Black-Scholes one-step simulation; payoff F(ST)=ST−K with K=1.5St.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Compute positive and negative payoff parts separately before amplitude estimation.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Combine the two estimated expectations to recover the final price.

speedup_claims.baseline_method: classical monte carlo / standard qamc with square-root encoding
speedup_claims.conditions: using separate estimation of positive and negative payoff parts
speedup_claims.caveats: This is still a workaround requiring two amplitude-estimation runs and recombination of results.

experiments.description: Direct encoding QAMC pricing of European-style derivatives using the direct payoff encoding and mIQAE on the simplified Black-Scholes setup.

algorithm.convergence_criteria: Target precision ϵ and confidence level 1−γ; mIQAE run until the desired precision is reached.

problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate discounted expected payoff E[F(ST)|Ft] by directly encoding the payoff amplitude and measuring the zero state probability after applying U†S UF US.

problem_instance.description: European vanilla call, vanilla put, and digital option pricing under Black-Scholes dynamics.

dataset_specification.description: Black-Scholes model with exact one-step simulation; no external dataset.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Discretize the Black-Scholes distribution into 32 points between 0.01 and 5.0; prepare the direct-encoding oracle UDE.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Estimate pricing error versus discretized expectation; report medians and 25/75 percentiles over repeated runs.

speedup_claims.conditions: direct encoding with mIQAE on European-style payoffs
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper states the impact of direct vs square-root encoding is minimal in practice.

experiments.description: Direct encoding combined with modified real quantum amplitude estimation (mRQAE) to price a negative-payoff linear derivative while recovering the sign of the expectation.

algorithm.convergence_criteria: Target precision ϵ and confidence level 1−γ; iterative interval shrinking until ϵ is reached.

problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate the signed expected payoff E[F(ST)|Ft] for a payoff that can be negative, using UDE and mRQAE to recover both magnitude and sign.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Iterative shift-and-amplify procedure; no decomposition into positive/negative parts required.

problem_instance.description: Linear payoff option with negative expectation example.

dataset_specification.description: Black-Scholes one-step simulation; payoff F(ST)=ST−K with K=1.5St.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Prepare the direct-encoding oracle UDE and the shifted oracles required by mRQAE; use the Black-Scholes discretization from the paper.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Recover the signed price estimate from the final confidence interval center; compare against discretized expectation.

classical_baselines.method_name: mIQAE with direct encoding and positive/negative decomposition

speedup_claims.factor: competitive with mIQAE; asymptotically optimal real amplitude estimation
speedup_claims.conditions: using direct encoding and iterative shift-and-amplify procedure
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper provides asymptotic bounds rather than a single empirical wall-clock speedup; performance depends on q, epsilon, and gamma.
